s3.isa_row.note: Date matches the aliyah date. Surname and Halisa address not legible in this copy - relying on Edo.

s3.married_in_cyprus.s: Miriam is listed under her maiden name in Cyprus (Jan 1948) and as Rosenblum in the aliyah database a year later -> married in Cyprus (Edo's inference).

s3.mendel_marriage_rec.s: Vicovu de Sus marriage 8.8.1922: Maidanek Mendel x Kurzberg Rosa; his parents Abraham & Chaje Odel Jurgrau; hers Meir & Henie Leah Rafael; bride born 12.12.1903; marriage record gives Mendel's birthplace as Vicovu de Sus.
s3.mendel_marriage_rec.note: Birthplace contradicts his own birth entry (D04: Oberhorodnik 476) - the birth entry wins. Bride's date 12.12 vs 13.12.1903 elsewhere.
val: Rosa's birth date 13.12.1903 confirmed by the births index; the marriage record's 12.12 is the outlier.

s3.mirjam_marriage.s: Vicovu de Sus 1.3.1922: Feldhammer Abraham x Majdanek Mirjam (same parents as Mendel).

s3.josef_1923.s: Josef, son of Mendel & Rosa: born 26.4.1923 house 397, died 29.9.1923 aged 5 months.
s3.josef_1923.note: Named after a deceased Josef - candidates: Rosa's brother Josef Kurzberg (b.1894) if he died before 1923.

s3.dona_jeni.s: Dona Jeni (Donzia), daughter of Mendel & Rosa, born 18.7.1924.
s3.dona_jeni.note: Not in the site or either knowledge base until now.

s3.vicov_deaths.s: Maidanek deaths in Vicovu de Sus 1913-1928 (per Edo): Hersch Rauchbach 1.11.1913; Adela née Druckmann 6.7.1914; Malka 21.11.1914; Mina Rauchbach 28.6.1915; infant 6.1.1921; Hersch Hechtenthal 12.2.1922; Scheindel aged 80, 13.8.1923; Hersch aged 82, 13.1.1928.
s3.vicov_deaths.note: The 13.1.1928 'Hersch aged 82' is in VICOVU DE SUS; our Hersch's stone says died 19.1.1928 in his 76th year. A civil date 6 days BEFORE the burial-stone date is odd, and Scheindel (80, d.1923) recalls the OTHER Hersch (son of Leiser, m. Scheindel Ostfeld 1881). Two Hersch Maidaneks dying in Jan 1928 is possible - check.

s3.rosenblum_kids_idx.s: Per Edo's indexes: Anna-Rose b.1907 (act 192); Meir b.25.2.1911 d.10.4.1911; Philip b.27.5.1912 (act 49); Eva b.27.12.1914 (act 2207).
val: Stage 11: Eva's act 2207 is confirmed on the image (D19, s3.eva_birth); Philip's 'act 49' looks wrong next to Fani's act 270 (22.2.1909) and Eva's 2207 (28.12.1914) - see s11.philip_act49_doubtful and X39. Anna-Rose's 192 untestable without her birth date.

s3.itzik_marriage.s: Itzik Rosenblum x Etla Offenberg, Iasi 22.11.1908, act 297; father Meir listed as deceased.
s3.itzik_marriage.note: Iasi, not Galati. The act should also name Taube (alive?) - check for her maiden name.

s3.emil_identity.s: Edo (7.10.2026): 'Emil' appears only on the Balta orphans list and in the family tree; community registers say Mendel.
s3.emil_identity.note: Contradicts the site's 'Mendel = Emil proven by his daughter's Page of Testimony'.

s3.mendel_fate.s: Edo: Mendel perished; named as father on the Balta orphans list (early 1944). No death record.
s3.mendel_fate.note: The site's 'murdered 1941 (PoT)' is not supported by anything in hand.

s3.mendel_occupation.s: No document in hand records Mendel's occupation (not in his marriage or his children's births).

s3.donors_1891_initials.s: 1891 donors in Vicovu de Sus include M. MAIDANEK, A. MAIDANEK and D. MAIDANEK (per Edo).
s3.donors_1891_initials.note: In 1891: A. = probably Abraham (20) - Adolf was ~5; D. = probably David (d.1900); M. = possibly Moshe (1914 council).
val: Dragusanul read in full: M., A. and D. MAIDANEK among 1891 donors.
Status per the published Roots site (rebuild had unchecked).

s3.speech_1910.s: 1910 speech in the Vienna parliament on the exploitation of Vicovu de Sus peasant forests names Maidanek among the speculators, with Eisenkraft and Flondor (per Edo, Dragusanul).
s3.speech_1910.note: Claude's own read of the Dragusanul page summarized the Laura-forest affair with Flondor, Eisenkraft and Druckmann - Maidanek mention to be verified.
val: Dragusanul quotes the 1910 report: 'Eisenkraft, Flondor şi Maidanek'.
Status per the published Roots site (rebuild had unchecked).

s3.cfr_1922.s: 1922 decree on timber stock for the CFR (railways) lists the Vicovu de Sus sawmill as property of Bodor & Filipescu - not Maidanek (per Edo, Dragusanul).
s3.cfr_1922.note: There may have been two sawmills, or the 1922 'Josef & Adolf' mention refers to something else.
val: Dragusanul: 'Fabrica din Vicovul de Sus. proprietatea dlor Bodor şi Filipescu' (1922).
Status per the published Roots site (rebuild had unchecked).

s3.mo1942_details.s: MO 154/1942: one guard of 'fabrica Maidanek' paid 2,000 lei/month (double the usual - a large site); appointments run Nov 1940 - Mar 1942 under the CNR, i.e. dispossession began late 1940 (per Edo).
s3.mo1942_details.note: Salary confirmed via Dragusanul; the Nov 1940-Mar 1942 period still to be checked on the MO scan.
val: Stage 8: the 'Nov 1940 - Mar 1942' appointment period is still not checked on the scan (only nos.198-199 captured, N17). The 1943 lease (S67) shows the owner of the factory was Iosif Maidanek, not Emil (s8.sawmill_not_emil).

s3.dad_firm_name.s: Dad's document: a sawmill 'Maidanek Josef & Adolf' in Vicovu de Sus appears c.1922, 1939 and 1941 in Romanian official records (MO citations not yet verified).
s3.dad_firm_name.note: Consistent with the 1929 firm 'Maidanek A. & I.' (S40). Adolf died Apr 1934, so the name outlived him.
val: Stage 8: Dad's document says 'Maidanek Josef & Adolf' c.1922, 1939 and 1941. The 1941 entry is verified (MO I 23/1941 no.168 'Adolf si Iosif Maidanek', s5.mo1941_firm); 1922 and 1939 are still unverified. The gazette order is Adolf first, then Iosif; Dad's document has Josef first.

s3.adolf_not_abraham.s: Adolf is not Abraham: Adolf died Apr 1934 aged 48 (born c.1886); Abraham was born 1871 and is 'Abraham' in 1898/1901 records.
s3.adolf_not_abraham.note: Refutes the 'Adolf = Abraham' hypothesis in the analysis Bar forwarded.
val: Read D01,D08. Refutes the 'Adolf = Abraham' hypothesis in the analysis Bar forwarded.

s4.hersch_birth.s: Births index: Maidanek Hersch, born Nov 1851; father Joel Maidanek; mother Taube Haber (registered 1875, book 1 p.83 no.22, IMG_5888).
s4.hersch_birth.note: PROVES Joel -> Hersch and Taube (née Haber) as his mother. Birth Nov 1851 fits the site (c.1851); the stone's '76th year' is off by one.
cit: Maidanek Hersch | F: Maidanek Joel | M: Haber Taube
val: Stage 15: register image IMG_5888 (W95-W98) read: Hersch b. Nov 1851 in Mardzina (Marginea), parents Joel Maidanek and Taube Haber, entered 2.4.1875 on an order of 29.3.1875.

s4.moses_1886.s: Births index: Maidanek Moses, born 1886 Oberwikow; father Hersch Maidanek; mother Nessie (née Herer); registered 1929 (book 13 p.135 no.135).
s4.moses_1886.note: Mendel's uncle. Late registration in 1929 (age 43). Born the same year as 'Adolf' (aged 48 in Apr 1934).
cit: Maidanek Moses | F: Maidanek Hersch | M: Maidanek Nessie | maiden Herer

s4.abraham_1884.s: Births index: Meidanek Abraham, born 15.11.1884 Oberwikow, son of Moses & Marie Meidanek (book 4 p.30 no.165).

s4.josef_1887.s: Births index: Meidanek Josef, born 12.5.1887, son of Moses & Marie Meidanek (book 4 p.114 no.70).

s4.sawmill_brothers.s: HYPOTHESIS: 'Maidanek A. & I.' (1929) / 'Josef & Adolf' = the brothers Abraham ('Adolf', b.1884) and Josef (b.1887), sons of Moses & Marie Meidanek of Oberwikow; their father Moses = the 1914 council member and sawmill owner.
s4.sawmill_brothers.note: Fits two brothers named A. and I./Josef, the Oberwikow location, and a well-off family (daughter married a Dr. in 1908). Tension: Adolf was 'aus Unter-Vicov' and '48' in Apr 1934 (Abraham would be 49). Alternative: Adolf = Moses b.1886, son of Hersch (Mendel's uncle). Decider: Adolf's 1934 death record (parents) or the firm file.
val: Stage 9 (7.10 20:00): the births index has no Adolf in any Meidanek/Maidanek family; Abraham b.15.11.1884 and Josef b.12.5.1887 (sons of Moses and Marie) are the only boys of the right age - see s9.adolf_is_abraham_1884. The brothers theory is now an inference (medium), no longer just a guess.

Stage 9 (7.10 20:00): the births index has no Adolf in any Meidanek/Maidanek family; Abraham b.15.11.1884 and Josef b.12.5.1887 (sons of Moses and Marie) are the only boys of the right age - see s9.adolf_is_abraham_1884. The brothers theory is now an inference (medium), no longer just a guess.

s4.chaje_odel_1905_besner.s: Births index (1905, Chane Freide): mother 'Maidanek Chaje Odel', maiden name indexed as BESNER - the likely origin of the site's 'née Besner'.
s4.chaje_odel_1905_besner.note: Edo: the 1905 entry calls her 'legitimate daughter of Chane Freide Besner'. The 1898, 1900, 1901, 1903 entries all say Jurgrau. So the site's error has a documentary source.

s4.chaje_odel_candidate_1879.s: Candidate only: births index has 'Jurgrau Chaie Hudie, born 1879, Ober Horodnik, mother Malke Jurgrau, father not mentioned', late-registered 1921 (book 11 p.401 no.217).
s4.chaje_odel_candidate_1879.note: Same village and the brother's year 1879; 'Hudie/Hodel/Odel' are one name. But the mother is Malke, not Chane Fride. Other Chaje Hudie Jurgraus: 1867, 1877, 1882.

s4.salomon_other_wives.s: Births index: a 'Salomon Jurgrau' had children with Feige (Edel) Fallenbaum 1877-1882 (Feige Jurgrau d.4.12.1888 aged 28) and with Lea Melzer 1889-1891 (civil marriage 26.9.1892). Same man as Chaje Odel's father? Unknown.
s4.salomon_other_wives.note: If the same Salomon, Chane Fride died c.1875-77 and Chaje Odel was born by then (1870 reading).
val: Pattern confirmed and extended: Feige (Edel) Fallenbaum children Beile 1.2.1877, Michael 17.10.1879, Chaje Hudie 16.4.1882 (Feige d.4.12.1888 aged 28); Lea Melzer children Keile 10.12.1889, Teme 3.8.1891, civil marriage 26.9.1892. Same-Salomon question stays open.

s4.jurgrau_1874_entry.s: Births index legitimation notes cite the 1874 marriage as 'vol. I, p.16/17, entry no. 41, 29.12.1874' - entry 41, not 20.
s4.jurgrau_1874_entry.note: Settles the entry-number discrepancy in earlier research notes.

s4.salomon_kids_births.s: Births index: Schloime Jurgrau & Chane (née Bösner): Jossel 11.8.1858, Marjim 20.11.1860, Debora 30.10.1862 - all legitimized by the 1874 marriage.
val: Full harvest reproduces the same children of Schloime x Chane (Bösner).

s4.michel_1863.s: Births index: Michel Jurgrau born 14.1.1863 to Chaim & Beile Jurgrau - Beile was still bearing children in 1863, consistent with the Beile who died 24.4.1866 aged 45.
s4.michel_1863.note: Upgrades the 1866 death to a probable match for Beile (J02).

s4.rosa_birth_ix.s: Births index: Kurzberg Rosa, born 13.12.1903, OBERWIKOW; father Meier, mother Heni Lea (née Raful) (book 6 p.259 no.234, P1100499).
s4.rosa_birth_ix.note: Settles conflict X05: born in Oberwikow (Vicovu de Sus); the register is Radautz's.

s4.kurz_children_ix.s: Births index, children of Meier (Wolf) Kurzberg & Heni Lea (Chane Lea / Babie) Raful, all Oberwikow: Josef 6.7.1894; Juda Leib 7.5.1896; twins Aron & Chane 15.6.1900; Rosa 13.12.1903; Debora 10.6.1905 (d.28.2.1906); MORTKO 30.12.1906 (mother's maiden name given as Hörer); twins Noa & Gisela 26.4.1912.
s4.kurz_children_ix.note: Nine children, not eight - Mortko is new.

s4.noe_children_ix.s: Births index: Noe Kurzberg & Ettie Golde Laufer - Mendel 8.6.1881 (d.19.1.1882), Marie 23.3.1884, both Oberwikow. Deaths index: Resi Ruchel Kurzberg d.25.4.1883 aged 4.
s4.noe_children_ix.note: Meir-Zeev's own birth is not in the index (born before consistent registration).

s4.raful_children_ix.s: Births index, children of Schaje (Moses) Reful/Refuel & Mariaße Hörer: Süßel 29.11.1871 (father 'Moses'), Schifra Chawe 17.3.1874, Chaim Simche 27.1.1876 (indexed as 'Rab/Rath'), Abraham Meier 8.6.1877 (d.28.5.1878), Ben Zion 31.5.1879 (father 'Schaje').
s4.raful_children_ix.note: Confirms the name 'Schaje Moses'. Heni Lea's own birth is not in the index.

s4.laufer_abr_chaim.s: Deaths index: Laufer Abr. Chaim, d. 19.2.1866, aged 76 (book 1 p.15 no.8, IMG_6973).
s4.laufer_abr_chaim.note: Confirms the site; my earlier page-scan missed it.

s4.laufer_lea_1899.s: Candidate: deaths index Laufer Lea, d. 7.9.1899, aged 80 (book 3 p.318 no.108) - b. c.1819, fits Etti-Golde's mother.

s4.laufer_marie_menze.s: Deaths index: Laufer Marie Menze, d. 2.8.1879, aged 24 (book 2 p.66 no.74).
s4.laufer_marie_menze.note: The site's 'Mari Mintze' - so she is not the Minzie Laufer who married Mechl Herer in 1881.

s4.leiser_marriage.s: Marriages index: Maidanek Leiser x Adelstein Sure, 18.10.1877 (book 2 p.1 no.5).

s4.maidanek_marriages_ix.s: Marriages index (Maidanek, 1870-1929): Moses x Marie Meidanek 13.1.1881; Hersch x Scheindel Ostfeld 25.1.1881; Abraham x Chaje Odel Jurgrau 3.10.1901; Mendel x Gitel Frime Winter 10.6.1903; Moses Mortko x Mali Weidenfeld 19.4.1906; Chaim Alter x Adela Drukmann 2.5.1906; Joel x Chaje Sure Zwik 28.7.1909. Brides: Silka x Salomon Dollberg 1877; Sossie x Chaim Locker 1881; Ettel x Aron Rauchbach 1884; Rifka x Josef Peritz 1900; Minzie x Manie Storfer 1901; Chaje Bince x Moses Schwitz 1904; Lina x Dr. Heinrich Arthur Tarden 1908; Malke Golde x Hoschia Tillinger 1909.
s4.maidanek_marriages_ix.note: No marriage for Abraham/Adolf (b.1884/1886) or Josef (b.1887) in the Radautz index - they married elsewhere or after 1929. Chaim Alter (David's son) x Adela Drukmann explains the 'Adela née Druckmann d.1914' in Vicov.
val: Stage 15: the entries 26, 27 and 29 of the January 1881 page are read in the image (W90-W94); the index is confirmed for Moses x Marie and Kurzberg x Laufer.

s4.maidanek_deaths_ix.s: Deaths index (Maidanek, 1857-1929) adds: Feibel aged 26 d.30.9.1867; Salomon 5m 1877; Awram Jankel 14 1878; Moses 8 1878; Feige, Chaskel, Marjem 1882; Scheindel 3 1885; Sime 1886; Leib 1887; Saul 1891; Osias 42 d.24.10.1901; Mariase 1908; Benzion b.19.1.1897 d.1.12.1928.
s4.maidanek_deaths_ix.note: Feibel (b.~1841) and 'Maidamach Rifke' (26, d.7.9.1867) may be a young couple - Feibel possibly a late son of Abraham-Yaakov.

s5.emil_pot.s: Yad Vashem PoT 5594110 (record 14010296), filed 15.4.1999 by his daughter Yehudit Gafni (nee Maidanek): Emil Meldel Maidanek, born Horodnik, father Avraham, mother Haika, wife Rosa nee Kurzberg, 3 children, lived Rădăuți; died of typhus at Ustia (Bershad district), Transnistria, 20.12 (form '1940', database 1941).
s5.emil_pot.note: PROVES Mendel = Emil (the same parents and wife as the 1898/1901/1922 records). 1940 on the form is impossible (deportation was Oct 1941); read 20.12.1941. CORRECTS my earlier verdict on X23.
cit: Emil Meldel Maidanek | father Avraham | mother Haika | wife Rosa Kurzberg

s5.mendel_pot2.s: Second PoT (1995978, Khava Shabat 1956): Mendel Meidanek b.1899 Horodnik, father Avraham, mother Khaia, lived Vicov, MERCHANT (סוחר), married, wife survived; died Obodovka camp 1941. A third PoT (957559, Zakharia Priling 1999): Mendel son of Avraham & Khaika, died Obodivka 1941.
s5.mendel_pot2.note: Three independent testimonies agree on parents and death in Transnistria Dec 1941. None calls him a sawmill owner; his sister-in-law calls him a merchant.

s5.avraham_pots.s: Three PoTs: Abraham Maidanek, son of Hersh, husband of Chaia/Khaika (nee Iurgrau), lived Horodnik; merchant (Khava Shabat 1956) / agriculturist (Zakharia Priling 1999); deported to Obodovka and died there 1941 (Priling: killed; Gafni: '1940').
s5.avraham_pots.note: Corrects 'died 1940 (per previous research)': died in Obodovka ghetto, winter 1941-42. PoT birth years 1877 vs register 1871 - register wins. Priling names his mother 'Ester' - against the 1901 marriage record and Frieda Gruber's 'Ite-Nesi Herer' (X29).

s5.chaje_pots.s: PoTs: Chaia Meidanek nee IURGRAU (575189, Khava Shabat 1956), wife of Avraham, Rădăuți, died Obodovka 1941; Khaika Meidanik (5630250 Priling; 5669697 Gafni), born Horodnic, died Obodovka 1941.
s5.chaje_pots.note: A 1956 testimony independently gives her maiden name as Jurgrau - one more nail in 'Besner'. Died Obodovka 1941, not 1940.
cit: Chaia | maiden name Iurgrau | spouse Avraham

s5.abraham_children_ix.s: Radautz births index, children of Abraham Maidanek & Chaje Odel Jurgrau: Mirjam 23.9.1896 Unterwikow (5/92/195); Mendel 26.3.1898 Oberhorodnik (5/186/59); Israel Mortko 18.2.1900 Oberhorodnik (5/332/28, d.25.5.1900); Chaim 13.6.1901 (5/418/110, surname 'Majdonek'); Joel 29.1.1903 (6/111/22, 'Maidonek'); Chane Freide 14.1.1905 (6/525/6). All legitimized/legitimate by the 3.10.1901 marriage.
s5.abraham_children_ix.note: Six children; four reached adulthood with known fates (Mendel, Chaim, Joel, Chane Freide = Anna). Israel Mortko's mother is 'Klara' Jurgrau = Chaje (Chaje = Klara).

s5.chaim_pot.s: PoT 369905 (his wife Khava Shabat, 1956): Chaim Meidanek, born 1901 Rădăuți, son of Avraham & Khaia, lived SELETIN, WOOD MERCHANT (סוחר עצים), wife Khava nee Nagel; died 1942 at Lucineț (Kopaygorod), Transnistria, aged 41.
s5.chaim_pot.note: Mendel's brother was in the timber trade.

s5.joel_pots.s: PoTs: Yoel Meidanek b.1903 Horodnik, son of Avraham & Khaia, single, CATTLE DEALER, lived Rădăuți, died Obodovka (Khava Shabat 1956; Priling 1999: died 1942). Gafni 1999 gives b.1911, age 29, died Ustia of disease.

s5.anna_pots.s: PoTs: Anna Ovaris nee Meidanek, b.1905 Horodnik, daughter of Avraham & Khaia, lived Czernowitz, married to Ovaris (survived); died Obodovka 1941 (Shabat) / 1942 (Priling). = Chane Freide b.14.1.1905.
s5.anna_pots.note: Anna is the civil form of Chane.

s5.mirjam_birth_ix.s: Births index: Mirjam Meidanek, born 23.9.1896 Unterwikow, father Abraham, mother Chaje Odel Jurgrau (5/92/195). No Yad Vashem record found for her.
s5.mirjam_birth_ix.note: Edo had 20.9.1896; the index says 23.9. She married Abraham Feldhammer 1.3.1922 (Vicovu de Sus, per Edo).

s5.mali_pots.s: Two PoTs (1999): Miriam Mali Priling/Frieling nee Maidanek, born 1893 Vicov, father Hersh/Tzvi Maidanek, mother Ite-Nesi Herer (Gruber) / 'Ester' (Priling), husband Arie Leib(ish), 5 children; deported Oct 1941 from Radautz; died of typhus in Obodovka (Dec 1941 / 1942).
s5.mali_pots.note: A new daughter of Hersch & Jitte Nesie: Abraham's sister, 22 years younger. Not in the Radautz births index (probably registered elsewhere or under another name).

s5.arie_sawmill.s: PoT 5630241 (son Zakharia, 1999): Arie Leibish Priling, born 1889 Oberwikow, son of Yitzhak; place of work: SAWMILL (מנסרת עצים); profession: CLERK (פקיד); wife Miriam nee Maidanek; died Obodovka 1942.
s5.arie_sawmill.note: The only testimony that mentions a sawmill: worked by Mendel's uncle-by-marriage, as an employee. It does not name the owner.
cit: מקום העבודה: מנסרת עצים | מקצוע: פקיד

s5.rosa_survivor.s: Survivors' registration form 4442342 (by daughter Yehudit Gafni): Roza Meidanik nee Kurtzberg, born 1904 Vicov, father Meir, mother Henia; wartime Vicov - Ustia - Obodovka - Balta ghetto; liberated Balta 1944; after the war Radautz; died 1980, Kiryat Motzkin.
s5.rosa_survivor.note: Settles I15: Rosa survived. Miriam was on the 'orphans' list because her father had died.
cit: father Meir | mother Henia | died 1980 Kiryat Motzkin

s5.miza_survivor.s: Survivors' registration form 4437000 (by her sister Yehudit Gafner/Gafni): Miza Meidanik, born 1928 Vicov, father Mendel, mother Roza; Vicov - Ustia - Obodovka - Balta ghetto; liberated Balta 1944; died 03/02/1999, Kiryat Motzkin.
s5.miza_survivor.note: Death date per her sister - family to confirm (03/02 read as 3 Feb, Israeli order). Birth year 1928 is against the register (16.5.1926) and the Cyprus list (1926) - X30.

s5.two_aunts.s: Family: Miriam had two sisters - Dontzia (Dona Jeni, b.18.7.1924) and Yeti (Jetti = Yehudit Gafni, b.~1931). They are two different people.
s5.two_aunts.note: Resolves L32. Emil's PoT '3 children' = Dontzia, Miza, Yeti (Josef d.1923 not counted). Dontzia's later life is unknown - not on Yad Vashem; ask the family.
cit: There are two aunts - Dontzia and Yeti

s5.yehudit_role.s: Yehudit Gafni nee Maidanek filed: PoT for her father Emil (1999), grandfather Avraham (2007), grandmother Khaika, uncle Joel (as niece), photo of Emil (2005), survivor forms for her mother Rosa and sister Miza.

s5.henia_pot.s: PoT 921888 (Genya Shalmuk, 20.2.1957): Henia Leja Kurzberg, born 1872 Radautz, father YESHAYAHU MOSHE, mother MIRIAM, husband Meir (died before the war), 8 children, residence Oberwikow, shop owner; died Transnistria 1942.
s5.henia_pot.note: Independent confirmation of her parents Schaje (Yeshayahu) Moshe & Mariaße (Miriam), and a birth year (1872) for I13.

s5.aharon_pots.s: PoTs: Ahron Kurzberg, born 1900 Oberwikow, son of Meir & Henia Lea, grocery-shop owner, wife Beilchi (b.1907 Vicovul de Sus), children Chaim 12, Mordechai Leib 8, Iti 6, Reizl 4 - all killed 1942 (Genya Shalmuk 1957). Second set (Klara Shvab 1957): Aharon, age 45, son of Meir & 'Baba', butcher, wife Berta 45, children Khaim 8, Leib 5, Eti 4, died Transnistria.
s5.aharon_pots.note: The memorial plaque on Meir's stone (Aharon, Beila, Chaim, Mordechai Leib, Yetti, Resi) is Aharon's family: the last four are his CHILDREN, not Rosa's siblings. 'Baba' = 'Babie', Heni Lea's name in the births index.

s5.mali_jurgrau_kurzberg.s: PoT 1133083: Mali Kurtzberg nee Jurgrau, born 1902 Rădăuți, married, died Djurin (Transnistria); filed by Tzipora Beiner. Husband not named - possibly the wife of one of Rosa's brothers (Josef 1894 / Juda Leib 1896).

s5.mo1941_firm.s: Monitorul Oficial I nr.23, 28.1.1941, p.427: Ministry of National Economy list of firms entitled to export in 1941 (replacing all 1940 lists) - no.168 'Adolf și Iosif Maidanek, Vicovul-de-Sus, jud. Rădăuți.'
s5.mo1941_firm.note: An official primary record of the firm's name in January 1941, months before the expropriation: ADOLF and IOSIF. s8.cnr_lease_1943.s: Monitorul Oficial, Partea a II-a, nr. 44, 22.2.1943, p.1017 (Centrul National de Romanizare, public tenders): the CNR announces a sealed-bid auction for 10.3.1943, 10 a.m., at its auctions service (str. Mantuleasa 42, Bucharest) for a 2-year lease of 'fabrica de cherestea, fosta Iosif Maidanek' (the sawmill, formerly Iosif Maidanek's) in the commune of Vicovul-de-Sus, Radauti county, from an annual rent of 365,000 lei; bidders must be of Romanian ethnic origin and deposit 10 percent of the two years' rent. This is Josef's name on the factory: after Adolf's death (April 1934) the sawmill is attributed to Iosif alone.
s8.cnr_lease_1943.note: Fourth official-gazette mention of the factory (after MO 1941 no.168, MO 1942 nos.198-199, and the 1929 list). The text layer reads 'Mdidanek'; the image (N16) reads Maidanek. 'fosta' = former: by Feb 1943 the factory had been taken from its Jewish owner and was being leased out by the state. It does not say which Iosif (n_josef_1887 is the standing candidate, s4.sawmill_brothers) nor whether other co-owners existed. Result of the 10.3.1943 auction not found. Decider: the CNR file at ANIC (L28).

s8.sawmill_firm_chain.s: One chain of records for the Vicovu de Sus sawmill, 1924-1943: 'Brueder / Gebrueder Maidanek' of Ober-Wikow, 2nd-largest sawmill at Vicov de sus with 15.1 wagons a month (Czernowitzer Morgenblatt 15.7.1924; donor lists 1924 and 1930) -> 'Maidanek A. & I.' (1929 list) -> 'Adolf si Iosif Maidanek, Vicovul-de-Sus' (export-licence list, MO 28.1.1941, no.168) -> 'fabr. Maidanek' expropriated and guarded by two state-paid guards (MO 6.7.1942) -> 'fabrica de cherestea, fosta Iosif Maidanek' leased out by the CNR (MO 22.2.1943). The owners named by the gazette are ADOLF (died April 1934) and IOSIF (Josef); the firm kept both names after 1934, and by 1943 the factory is Iosif's alone.
s8.sawmill_firm_chain.note: 'Partly' because the link between the German press's 'Brueder Maidanek' and the gazette's 'Adolf si Iosif' rests on place, names and an unbroken run of dates (same village, same two first names, 1924-1943), not on a record that says 'brothers' - the gazette gives only the firm name. Strong inference, not stated in any single record. A second inference: Josef Maidanek was substitute INDUSTRY delegate beside the sawmill owner Josef Surkes (Straja sawmill, 1924 wagon list) on the Radauti tax-appeal commission 1936-37, so he was a timber industrialist (s6.josef_1937). Whether this Josef is n_josef_1887 stays a separate hypothesis (s4.sawmill_brothers).

s8.sawmill_not_emil.s: Dad's question, answered so far: Emil (Mendel) Maidanek did NOT own the Vicovu de Sus sawmill. The gazette names the firm's owners as Adolf and Iosif (1941) and Iosif alone (1943); in the press Emil is a separate merchant ('Maidanek Emil, Kaufmann, Oberwikow', 1928) and his own donation ('Emil Maidanek 65') is listed apart from 'Brueder Maidanek' (1930). He was also deported and died in Transnistria on 20.12.1941 (s5.emil_pot), i.e. before the July 1942 guard list and the 1943 lease (the expropriation itself may date from late 1940-41, s3.mo1942_details). Whether Adolf and Josef were his relatives at all is NOT settled (s8.kinship_still_open).
s8.sawmill_not_emil.note: An inference from absence: Emil's name is in none of the gazette entries and the press lists him apart from the firm. A silent partner cannot be excluded from lists that print only registered names; the trade-register file (L28) would close it. Supersedes the open reading in L23 ('answer so far: NO').

s8.kinship_still_open.s: Who were Adolf and Josef to Emil? STILL OPEN. None of about 110 pages with 'Maidanek' (DiFMOE 1919-1941, Die Stimme 1956-2000, Hauster) names the father, wife or children of Adolf or Josef, or says what they were to Emil or to his father Abraham; no search found 'Joseph', 'Moses', 'Marie', 'Adolf und Josef', 'A. & J. Maidanek' or 'Maidanek & Co'. What the sources DO show: Adolf and Josef were the sawmill firm; Emil was a separate merchant in the same village.
s8.kinship_still_open.note: Age arithmetic (not evidence): Emil was born in 1898 and his father Abraham in 1871, whereas Adolf was about 48 in April 1934 (b. c.1886) and the candidate Josef was born in 1887 - so neither can be Emil's BROTHER (the inbox note F16 says 'Emil's brother is possible'; on the KB's dates (Abraham b.1871 would have been 15) it is not, unless Abraham's year is wrong). They could be his uncles (sons of Hersch, like Moses b.1886) or more distant cousins (e.g. sons of Moses & Marie). Deciders: Adolf's 1934 death record (L42), the firm file at SJAN Suceava and the CNR file at ANIC (L28), Josef's and Fany's later fate (L50).

s8.meir_oren_brother_doubt.s: the family tree (s6.dad_rosenblum_sibs) makes Meir Oren (Rosenblum) Peretz's BROTHER, but Peretz's father was himself Meir Rosenblum, already dead on 1.7.1906 ('Meer Rosemblum defunct', D02) - and Peretz (b.1879) has a known brother Itzik (1908 marriage). Ashkenazi families name children after the dead, not the living, so a son Meir born while his father Meir was alive is unlikely (a posthumous son would be the exception). HYPOTHESIS, not evidence: Meir Oren is a NEPHEW or cousin of Peretz (e.g. a son of Itzik or of another brother, named for the grandfather), or the family tree is wrong.

The 1947 summons is in Part II ('Partea a 2-a'), so any later court notice is in Part II too - Part III in these years is not where court notices sit. Issues the search engine associated with the query (all UNREAD, Part II unless noted): 1945-05-19 nr.111; 1945-06-21 nr.138; 1945-09-14 nr.209; 1946-03-06 nr.55; 1946-05-28 nr.122; 1947-11-20 nr.269; 1947-12-09 nr.285; Part I 1946-11-08 nr.260, 1941-06-13 nr.137, 1944-11-14 nr.264; for 'Valeanu Eva' Part I 1945-08-27 nr.193 and 1947-10-16 nr.239. Only 1947-11-20 nr.269 and 1947-12-09 nr.285 post-date the summons and are court-notice issues, so they are the first two to open. If no judgment was published, it sits in the court file (Ilfov Tribunal Dos. 92/1947 - the SMBAN email draft).

s8.galati_exodus_figures.s: Galati Jewish population: 13,000 in 1947, 9,000 in 1950, 450 in 1969 (KehilaLinks Galati history page), so the exodus ran through the whole period 1947-1969, not only 1948-52 (W1 F8 gave the same figures). Pinkas HaKehillot Romania (Galati) names no post-1944 individuals; it says only that Bessarabian refugees in Galati mostly went to Eretz Israel after the war. HYPOTHESIS (low): Peretz was a carpenter (peretz.1), so a craftsmen's landsmanshaft in New York - the Galatzer Handwerker KUV Society (Mount Hebron Cemetery, Queens) - is the kind of body relatives might have joined; JOWBR covers Romanian landsmanshaft cemeteries (L55).

s9.adolf_is_abraham_1884.s: HYPOTHESIS (inference): 'Adolf' Maidanek of Oberwikow (d. April 1934) is Abraham Meidanek, b. 15.11.1884 Oberwikow, son of Moses and Marie - a secular name used for the Hebrew name Avraham. Evidence: (1) the Radautz births index (12,130 births of the Radautz, Solca and Vicov Jewish communities 1857-1929) contains NO child named Adolf in any Meidanek/Maidanek family, although Adolf was born c.1885-86; (2) the only boys of that age in the family are Abraham (15.11.1884) and Josef (12.5.1887), both sons of Moses and Marie of Oberwikow; (3) the firm's partners are 'A. & I.' (1929), 'Adolf si Iosif' (1941), 'Brueder' (1924), i.e. Adolf and Iosif were brothers working together, and Josef b.1887 fits Iosif; (4) Adolf for Avraham is attested (JewishGen's example 'Avraham hamechune Adolf'). Against: the 1934 obituary says aged 48, while Abraham was 49 years 5 months in April 1934 (a one-year slip is common in press notices); and it is not a standard pairing.
s9.adolf_is_abraham_1884.note: Resolves the old worry 'Adolf is not Abraham' (X26, s3.adolf_not_abraham): that was about Emil's father Abraham b.1871 (d. Obodovka 1941), a different man. This is a third Abraham, b.1884. What would prove it: Adolf's 1934 civil death record (age, parents - L42), a birth or marriage record that gives both names, or a family document. Until then: probable, not proven.

s9.moses_kin_unproven.s: Are Moses and Marie Meidanek (parents of Adolf = Abraham and Josef) related to Emil's line? STILL UNPROVEN; the hints are only: the same rare surname in the same village (Oberwikow); Moses married Marie (also a Meidanek) on 13.1.1881, and in the next entry (no.27) Moses's own sister Sossie (daughter of Leiser and Sure, not Marie's sister) married Chaim Locker (CORRECTION, stage 14: an earlier version also counted the twelve days before the marriage of Hersch Maidanek and Scheindel Ostfeld, 25.1.1881, as a hint; that Hersch is another man, the son of Leizer - see s14.hersch_1881_other_man - so the coincidence is void); the Vicov donor list of 1891 shows M., A. and D. MAIDANEK (Dragusanul); a son named Abraham in 1884 could honour the dead Abraham-Yaakov (d.1860, Hersch's grandfather) - weak. HYPOTHESIS: Moses is a brother or first cousin of Hersch (b.1851, son of Joel and Taube). If a brother: Adolf and Josef are first cousins of Emil's father Abraham (b.1871) and first cousins once removed of Emil. No record says so.
s9.moses_kin_unproven.note: What would settle it: Moses's own birth or death record (he was born before the index starts in 1857, so look for his marriage act of 1881, which names his parents; Edgar Hauster can photograph it - see the 'Request Record' link), Adolf's 1934 death act, or any family document. Practical: ask Dad whether anyone ever said 'we had cousins with the sawmill'; and ask SJAN Suceava / Edgar Hauster for the 1881 marriage act of Moses x Marie (book P1120788) - it should give both fathers.

s10.sahgf_427_klara.s: Line 427 of the SAHGF list of Romanian immigrants who reached Palestine on 11 January 1945 reads: ROSENBLUM Klara, age 21, father Leo, mother Fanny, country Romania, birthplace Cernauti (Czernowitz). This is almost certainly Klara Wagner nee Rosenblum (b. Czernowitz 7.4.1923; wife of Moses Hirsch Wagner, citizenship application 1946, Israel State Archives 00146l7): age 21 in January 1945 fits b. April 1923, and the birthplace fits. She is NOT Yehuda's sister Klara of Galati, whose parents were Peretz and Liza - this Klara's parents are Leo and Fanny.

s11.claims_conference_db.s: The JewishGen 'Romania, Claims Conference' database is a Holocaust-era name list: 167,815 Romanian Jews whose names appear in records of the Central Zionist Archives (and, per USHMM, Yad Vashem). Entries may carry name, birth date and place, place of internment, source document and a Claims Conference remark; the page gives no date range and says nothing about post-war residence or emigration, so it can place a sibling (e.g. Philip, a forced labourer in Galati in 1942) before 1945 but not after. The same index is searchable WITHOUT a login in the USHMM Holocaust Survivors and Victims person search (source id 20684). The database itself was NOT searched.
s11.claims_conference_db.note: Confirmed as a description of the resource only. Route to run it: lead L72 (USHMM on Bar's Mac) or L55 (JewishGen login).

s11.romania_100_year_rule.s: The IGRA 'Resource Guide: Romania' (= JewishGen InfoFile by Marcel Glaskie, Ra'anana, 7.12.2017) says civil registers older than 100 years are held in the county archives and open, newer ones only to proven family members. If that rule holds, in 2026 EVERY Galati birth up to 1926 is open to an ordinary request - Anna-Rose (1907), Philip (1912), Sali and Klara (born between 1915 and 1923?) and Yehuda (1924) - and the margins of the birth acts record later marriages (Eva's margin gives the 1941 marriage to Valeanu). Fani's act (D06, act 270/1909) shows no margin note on the image in the file; Eva's does. The guide has nothing on Galati, on post-1945 emigrants or on landsmanshaftn.
s11.romania_100_year_rule.note: Medium: the rule comes from a tool summary of a short guide and the 'up to 1926' reading is mine. The practical step is the archive request in lead L67.

s11.ushmm_rg25030m_galati_lists.s: The post-1944 Galati archive holds named Jewish lists that fit the siblings question - USHMM RG-25.030M (63 reels, 51,350 images, 1940-1953): (a) Comitetul Democratic Evreiesc Galati (Fond 870, Inv. 957, reels 27-35), file 19, 1950-1952, 183 pp., 'Tabele nominale cu evidenta pe regiune a celor care au solicitat sa plece in Israel'; (b) same fond, file 34, 1951-1952, 199 pp., members' tables, references and autobiographies; (c) Comunitatea evreilor din Galati (Fond 643, reel 38), file 5, 1946, 'Tabele nominale cu evreii care au primit ajutoare la Comunitatea Evreilor din Galati'; (d) Prefectura Covurlui files 14/1945 and 21/1945 (repatriates from the USSR). If a sibling stayed in Galati until the 1950-52 Israel wave, file 19 is where the name and address would be; the 1946 aid list also shows who was in Galati and poor in 1946. The images are not online (Museum reading room or on-campus stations only). Whether any sibling is in them is unknown.
s11.ushmm_rg25030m_galati_lists.note: High that the files exist; unchecked what they contain. Not a browser job: email the USHMM reference desk (look-up or copies for Rosenblum / Volman / Finkelstein) and SJAN Galati, which holds the originals (Fond 870 and Fond 643). Lead L63.

s11.galati_landsmanshaft.s: Galati landsmanshaft trail, checked: the only Galati society found is the 'Galatzer Handwerker KUV Society' at Mount Hebron Cemetery (Queens, New York), 'established in New York by immigrants from Galati'; the Mount Hebron page names no members, plots or years. The AJHS landsmanshaft catalog has no society with Galati in its name (Romanian societies are filed as 'United Rumanian Jews of America'); the Center for Jewish History Romania guide names YIVO landsmanshaftn from Bacau, Birlad, Botosani, Bucharest, Burdujeni, Radauti, Satu Mare, Bereg, Bukovina and Maramures, not Galati. Nothing found for Montreal, Toronto, Chicago or Tel Aviv. HYPOTHESIS (low): Peretz was a carpenter, so a craftsmen's society is the plausible one for a sibling who went to New York; no evidence that any sibling did.
s11.galati_landsmanshaft.note: Low yield: Mount Hebron burial search (if public) for the society's section, then JOWBR for Rosenblum / Volman burials in that section.

s11.sali_misha_hypothesis.s: HYPOTHESIS (low), about Sali and Misha: Misha is a Russian-style first name, and Galati had many refugees from Bessarabia and Bukovina who mostly went to Israel (Pinkas HaKehillot, s8.galati_exodus_figures). Sali may therefore have married a Bessarabian or Soviet man and lived in the USSR or Moldova after 1940, and Misha may be a Soviet-born cousin who reached Israel, the US or Germany in the 1970s-90s. No record. Stage 6 also suggests 'Sali' may be Anna-Rose's family name (Anna-Rose is not in the family tree). Dad's Geni export shows, below Sali (deceased), only Misha and his descendants, all without surnames; Fani has the married name VOLMAN, birthplace 'Galaz' and no spouse; Philip's wife appears only as 'Liza' with the married name Rosenblum (no maiden name); Eva and Klara have no spouse or children. Living people: name and relationship only.

s11.philip_act49_doubtful.s: Doubt about Edo's index number for Philip's birth: s3.rosenblum_kids_idx gives 'act 49' for Philip b. 27.5.1912, but Fani's act was no. 270 on 22.2.1909 (D06) and Eva's no. 2207 on 28.12.1914 (D19). s13.yehuda_1925_not_1924.s: Yehuda was born on 21 January 1925, not 1924. the family tree (and the Geni profile it came from) says 21.1.1924; the civil certificate says 21.1.1925 and the register entry is dated 22.1.1925. The 1924 is probably a family or profile error of one year. Consequences: he was 23 in the Cyprus camp (1948) and 24 at his marriage (1949); his siblings were 2-18 years older.

s14.hersch_1881_other_man.s: CORRECTION. The Hersch Maidanek who married Scheindel Ostfeld on 25.1.1881 (Radautz marriages index) is NOT Emil's grandfather. Emil's grandfather Hersch (Zvi, b. Nov 1851, son of Joel and Taube Haber, d. 19.1.1928) had his children with Jitte-Nesie Herer from Abraham (b.1871) to Mali (b.1893), and Jitte-Nesie lived until 1928, five years after the Scheindel of the 1881 marriage died (13.8.1923, aged 80, Vicovu de Sus). So the 1881 bridegroom is the other Hersch, son of Leizer and Sarah (Edo's claim hersch.5; stage 3 note on the 'two Hersch' deaths of January 1928). Consequence: the earlier remark that Moses Meidanek married Marie 'twelve days before Hersch, Emil's grandfather' (STATUS 7-8 Oct, s9.moses_kin_unproven) was wrong and is withdrawn; the date coincidence is no hint of kinship.
s14.hersch_1881_other_man.note: Found by the WRITER while refreshing the deliverables (8.10 08:00). Inference rather than a record: it rests on Jitte-Nesie Herer being Emil's grandmother and Hersch's only wife in the records (cl.jite_alive_1901, s4.hersch_birth) - the 1881 marriage act would settle it by naming the bridegroom's parents (Leizer and Sarah vs Joel and Taube). What remains of the kinship case for Moses: the same rare surname in the same village, the 1891 donor initials, and the name Abraham (see s9.moses_kin_unproven).

s15.moses_son_of_leiser_putna.s: ANSWER TO LEAD L58. The Radautz marriage register, vol. s15.marie_father_is_david_1876.s: Marie's father David Maidanek of Radautz is, very probably, the David Maidanek (born c.1826, died 1900 in Unterwikow, a widower) who married Devora Rosenberg on 6.6.1876 in Radautz (house 609) and whom the 1876 marriage index calls the son of Abraham and Mindel Maidanek (parents from Zaleszczyk, Galicia). For: the same two first names (David and Dwora / Devora) in the same town (Radautz), the same rare surname, fitting ages (David b.c.1826, Devora 48 in 1876 so b.c.1828, Marie b.c.1858), and David acts as godfather in 1884 and 1887. Against or open: the civil marriage of 1876 came 18 years after Marie's birth, so it is probably a late legalisation of a religious marriage (in 1875 Hersch's birth was also entered late on an order), or a second marriage with Dwora named as stepmother; the act of 6.6.1876 (images IMG_5417 / IMG_5423 / IMG_5426, vol. 1 p.28 no.78) will say.
s15.marie_father_is_david_1876.note: Next: read the 1876 act (P9, first priority) - it names David's parents and Devora's, and Marie's name may appear.

s15.kinship_adolf_josef_probable.s: ANSWER (probable, not proven) TO BAR'S QUESTION 'WERE ADOLF AND JOSEF OUR RELATIVES?'. Adolf (= Abraham b.1884) and Josef (b.1887), the sawmill brothers, are the sons of Moses and Marie. Marie was the daughter of David Maidanek of Radautz; David was the son of Abraham and Mindel Maidanek (1876 index), and Emil's great-grandfather Joel is 'ben Avraham-Yaakov' on his grave record, Mindel being documented only as David's mother. If David and Joel are brothers (sons of the Abraham-Yaakov who died in Radautz in 1860), then Marie is a first cousin of Hersch (Emil's grandfather), and Adolf and Josef are second cousins of Emil's father Abraham (b.1871) and second cousins once removed of Emil (Mendel). The kinship runs through their MOTHER; on the father's side Moses is a son of Leiser of Putna and no link to Joel is shown (Leiser's father is unknown). The sawmill itself is not Emil's (s8.sawmill_not_emil): it belonged to his probable second cousins.
s15.kinship_adolf_josef_probable.note: Weak points: (1) David is only presumed to be the husband of Devora (1876); (2) the Abraham of David's father and the Abraham-Yaakov of Joel's grave are presumed the same man (same generation, same town, same surname, but no document links them); (3) Joel's own parents are not named in any record seen. What would close it: the 1876 act (David's parents), Joel's marriage or a birth of one of his children with grandparents, a cemetery record of David, and the 1877 act of Leiser (the Putna side). Practical for Dad: 'very probably yes, as cousins through Marie'.

s15.leiser_putna_hint.s: A geographic hint for the Putna side, not a proof: Joel was born in Karlsberg (Gura Putnei, 'mouth of the Putna'), Leiser was the rabbi of Putna, and Leiser's son Moses (c.1857) and Joel's son Hersch (1851) were both born in Mardzina (Marginea). Joel (b. c.1829) and Leiser (children born 1855-57) are of the same generation, so Leiser is a brother, cousin or other close relative of Joel - or unrelated neighbours with the same rare surname.
s15.leiser_putna_hint.note: Needs a document: Leiser's own marriage act (18.10.1877, book 2 p.1 no.5) and the 1881 act of the other Hersch name his father; Leiser's father = Abraham-Yaakov would make Leiser Joel's brother (lead L87).

s15.leiser_sure_1877_tension.s: TENSION to resolve: the marriage index lists Leiser x Sure Adelstein on 18.10.1877 (book 2 p.1 no.5), but the 1881 act names Sure as the mother of Sossie (b. c.1855) and Moses (b. c.1857), and Edo's tree names 'Sara' as Leiser's wife. A marriage entered in 1877 cannot be the first marriage of the parents of children born in 1855-57 - unless it is a late civil registration (as for David in 1876 and for Hersch's birth in 1875), or Sure was a second wife who is named as mother in 1881. Also open: whether Sure Adelstein and Edo's 'Sara' are one woman.
s15.leiser_sure_1877_tension.note: The 1877 act (lead L87) should show age and previous marital status of both.

s15.haganah_reply_2026_10_08.s: The Haganah Historical Archives (IDF and Defense Establishment Archives, Tel Aviv) answered Bar's inquiry on 8.10.2026: the archive holds documentation about the clandestine-immigration ships, but the LISTS OF MA'APILIM are kept in the Central Zionist Archives in Jerusalem. It suggests that Bar (1) fills in the attached Request for Use Form, (2) contacts the Organization of Cyprus Ma'apilim, and (3) writes to two researchers it names (Prof. Snunit Shoham, Dr. Aki Segev Miller). So the passenger list of the Atzmaut / Kibbutz Galuyot (Yehuda's passage from Cyprus, 1948-49) is probably in the Central Zionist Archives, not at the Haganah.
s15.haganah_reply_2026_10_08.note: The form asks for the applicant's passport or ID number, phones and address: Bar fills it himself (purpose: Family History; subject: Yehuda Rosenblum, Cyprus camp 63, ship Atzmaut or Kibbutz Galuyot, 1948-49). s16.philip_1951_immigration.s: Philip (Filip) Rosenblum, b.27.5.1912 Galati, son of Peretz Rosenblum and Liza nee Finkelstein, immigrated to Israel in March-April 1951: ISA immigrant list gl-15496-4, p.47, entry #1008, ID 26392. He immigrated alone (no wife/children on his row); occupation and destination columns still unread. This is the first hard trace of any of Yehuda's siblings after 1945.
s16.philip_1951_immigration.note: Dad said 9.10: Philip married Liza, died Israel, buried Kiryat Bialik, no children. Naturalization/registration file (ID 26392) is the next step - email 24 to ISA in flight (reply-watch).

s16.mendel_kurzberg_1951.s: Mendel Kurzberg: b.1906, parents David/Pesia, from Romania, destination , immigrated March-April 1951: ISA gl-15496-4, entry #1100, ID 21812 (same volume as Philip). the family tree has NO David/Pesia Kurzberg, so no relation to Rosa nee Kurzberg can be established from the tree; stays HYPOTHESIS that he belongs to the same Romanian Kurzberg cluster.
s16.mendel_kurzberg_1951.note: No open-web trace in Israel (Hebrew/English, 9.10.2026). Next: BillionGraves/GraveZ  (lead L94); naturalization file could be folded into the ISA email 24 reply-watch.

s18.chunne_acquittal_1930.s: Chunne (Chune) Ellenbogen was ACQUITTED on 5 June 1930: the Radautz tribunal acquitted all 38 defendants in the 'Geheimbündlerprozeß' on all charges - 'Es gab keine einzige Verurteilung, denn keiner der fünf Anklagepunkte konnte durch irgend welche konkrete Beweise erhärtet werden.' The prosecutor announced an appeal (Berufung/Rekurs); the appeal's outcome is not traceable. The 38 (workers, employees, merchants, craftsmen) were accused under the 1924 'lex Marzescu' emergency law of secret association and communist propaganda for belonging to the dissolved workers' sports club 'Rapid'.

s19.pan_sailing_27dec.s: The Pan York and Pan Crescent sailed together from Burgas on 27 December 1947 (CORRECTED from 26 December per the 22:50 follow-up; matches Edo's route), were boarded unopposed by the British on 31 December 1947 and reached Cyprus on 1 January 1948, with 15,000+ Romanian and Bulgarian Jewish ma'apilim. The ships stayed anchored off Bogaz for five months while people were moved ashore.
s19.pan_sailing_27dec.note: W4d findings 1 + 22:50 correction. Four sources agree on the timeline.
cit: cyprsii.org.il Pan page; palyam.org 'Stranded in Bogaz'

s19.pan_renames.s: The two ships were renamed twice: mid-voyage Ben-Gurion gave them the Hebrew names Kibbutz Galuyot (Pan York) and Atzmaut (Pan Crescent); after independence Pan York was renamed Komemiut. When searching passenger lists, try all names: Pan York, Pan Crescent, Kibbutz Galuyot, Atzmaut.
cit: 'קיבוץ גלויות' ל'פאן יורק' ו'עצמאות' ל'פאן קרסנט'

s19.karaolos_camps.s: The Pan ships' ma'apilim were detained at Karaolos (summer camps 55, 60, 61, 62 and 63), about 2 km northwest of Famagusta's old city. Pan York carried 7,557 passengers, Pan Crescent 7,612 (first-hand and ship-list sources). Avi Livney's testimony: Pan York passengers went first to the Xylotimbou winter camps while others cut their way into the Karaolos camps.
cit: camps 55/60/61/62/63 ~2km NW of Famagusta old city

s19.cyprus_numbers.s: After independence the two Pan ships ferried about 30,000 freed Cyprus inmates to Israel in July 1948; the last detainees left Cyprus in January-February 1949. Yad Vashem: 52,000 Jews passed through the Cyprus camps between 13 Aug 1946 and 10 Feb 1949, taken off 39 boats; about 2,200 babies were born in the camps.
s19.cyprus_numbers.note: W4d finding 4; T11. Brackets Yehuda and Miriam's arrival window (Atzmaut ~9.2.1949).

s20.axelrad_sawmill.s: The 'Holzindustriefirma V. Axelrad' of Vicovul de Sus owned its own sawmill - a SECOND Vicov sawmill besides the Maidanek brothers'. In 1927 the firm was to transport 7,500 kg of Decouville narrow-gauge rails from Brodina to its sawmill; the shipment was confiscated en route as alleged Austro-Hungarian army war booty. The firm proved private purchase with its own funds, the criminal case was dropped, and the court heard its damages claim (concluded 6.2.1937). The 'V.' initial is unresolved - likely Hersch/Mechel Axelrad's firm (or an OCR artifact); the Maidaneks were ~7x larger (1924: Brüder Maidanek 15.1 wagons/month vs Hersch Axelrad 2 wagons/month).
s20.axelrad_sawmill.note: Q507 (R1+R2), Q515, Q524. The Jakobeny sawmill fire ('Ferma Goldenzweig, Scheuermann u. Axelrad') is a DIFFERENT Axelrad in a different town - not the Vicov firm.
cit: 'Im Jahre 1927 hatte die Holzindustriefirma V. Axelrad aus Vicovul de sus eine Quantität von 7.500 Kilogramm Decouville-Schmalspurbahnschienen aus Brodina in das Sägewerk der Firma nach Vicov de sus zu transportieren.'

Vorrat). 2 Waggons monatlich' 10.7.1924 (Allgemeine); 1935 Kultusrat Liste 1 ('Hersch Axelrad (Vicov de sus)'); 1937 Dornești trade commission ('Handel: Hersch Axelrad, Berisch Groß'). He was also a trader ('Mechel Axelrad, Alfred Lewin' Gurahumorului) and earlier a tavern keeper ('Schänker in Vicovul de Sus', witness at a 1922 wedding). No press trace after 1937.
cit: 'Vicov de sus: .. Kersch Axelrad (670 Kg. Vorrat), 2 Waggon, monatl.'

s20.anna_besner_anomaly.s: ANOMALY: Anna Besner (b.23-Jul-1891, P1110070) has father Mendel Besner but mother listed as 'Chewed Korber' - while all her siblings' mother is Sluwe Devora Habermann. s20.karoline_horer.s: Salomon Weisler (Schulem) married Karoline Horer on 6-Sep-1883 (marriage index #321, act P1120795). The 1883 marriage act says the maiden name is HÖRER; the daughters' birth entries spell it 'Herer' (1891) and 'Hörer' (1897). 'Herer' is a distinct large Radautz family (100+ birth entries 1854-1926, multiple branches: Efroim x Regina; Abraham x Malke Wagner; Pinkas x Hendel Hechtling; Michel x Mina), NOT spelling instability - and the families intermarried (Hörer Moses b.8-Feb-1881, father Hörer Itzig, mother Herer Frime). The 1891 'Herer' for Karoline is most likely a clerk's confusion between the two similar surnames; the marriage act (primary document) wins. The act images (P1120795, P1110066) would show the original handwriting. Karoline's own parentage is open - the 1883 act names her parents (the Seide-Karoline bridge, standing pull list).

Yet he has NO birth or marriage in the Radautz/Solca/Vicov indexes (1857-1929) - born before 1857 or outside the indexed communities. He is very likely of Karoline Horer's (m.1883) generation - possibly a brother or cousin - but unproven.

s20.leib_wolfram_robbery.s: Leib Gerschon Wolfram (b.~1868) was a substantial Oberwikow grocer-merchant (Greisler): he owned a big house in the village center where he had run a grocery store for many years, flat attached. On 3-Nov-1932, around midnight, four masked rifle-armed bandits broke in, dragged the 64-year-old from bed, beat him terribly with rifle butts (severe injuries), stole 12,000 Lei from a hiding place plus 20,000 Lei of shop goods, and carted them off in a waiting wagon (the same gang suspected in a recent Falcău robbery). Follow-up 2.12.1932: additional loot - Austrian silver coins (5 fl., 2 K, 1 Kr.), Russian silver coins, a gold ladies' wristwatch. No trial or arrest coverage found (DiFMOE 0).
s20.leib_wolfram_robbery.note: Q506, Q516. Leib d. after Nov 1932. His birth (~1868) and parentage are not in the indexed births (pre-1857 coverage); the DAChO marriage act (~1886) would name his parents.

s20.putna_dollbergs.s: The Putna Dollbergs were a timber-merchant family active in KKL and community giving through the 1920s-30s: 'Brüder Dollberg' (Dollberg Brothers) timber firm - 1500 kg production, 26 kg stock, 4.5 wagons monthly (Morgenblatt 13.7.1924) + Saul Dollberg (670 kg stock, 2 wagons monthly, same stats; also a 3.7.1923 school-fund donor); KKL/donor lists 1924-1930 naming Wolf, Markus, Noe/Noa, Josef, Max, W. jun., Jakob, Saul, Feibl, Seide Besler, Isak, I., O., N., Rosa, Estera Dollberg (1924: 'Salzberger - Dollberg' KKL committee; 1925: Noe, Josef, Max, W. jun., Jakob; 1926: Rosa collector, Dina collector; 1930: W., N., O., I., Isak). Estera Dollberg of Putna died mid-July 1938 after long suffering ('Todesfall. Dieser Tage starb in Putna nach langem Leiden Frau Estera Dollberg.. Um Frau Dollberg trauern zwei Söhne, und zwar Ingenieur Dollberg, der technische Leiter der Zementfabrik an Putna und ein anderer Sohn, der Advokat ist.' - Morgenblatt 19.7.1938). Her husband is not named; her age is not given. The lawyer is likely 'Adv. Dr. M. Dollberg, Vatra-Dornei' (19 DiFMOE items 1923-1937 - the ONLY Dollberg lawyer in the region; given name never spelled out) - hypothesis medium; the engineer's given name is unknown (Heinrich Dollberg b.1912 hypothesis, medium).
s20.putna_dollbergs.note: Q508, Q561, Q562, Q563, Q566, Q568. Sibling/cousin relationships among the Putna Dollbergs are not stated in any item.

s20.putna_registers.s: METHOD FINDING: there is no separate Putna register gap - Putna (jud. Rădăuți) Jews registered births in Radautz. The reisch-cache birth index ShowDetails view carries a birthplace column ('Putna' / 'Putna jud. Radautz' / 'Unterwikow' - e.g. 'P1110181','8-Mar-1882','Putna' for Moses Dolberg; 'P1110181','20-Dec-1892','Unterwikow' for Wolf Dollberg). The JewishGen Bukovina resources page lists Suceava State Archives Jewish holdings for Radauti, Suceava, Gura Humorului, Cimpulung, Vatra Dornei, Burdujeni - NO Putna. The 1906 Joßel Alter x Ester Zwiebel marriage (P1120725, Radautz index) fits the same pattern. This RESOLVES X49: R6 Q575's 'no birthplace column' refers to the list view; the ShowDetails view does carry birthplace.

s20.dina_dollberg.s: Dina Dollberg (Putna community collector, Aug 1926 - paired with Isak Salzberg; 'Putna. d. Dina Dollberg - Isak Salzberg', OJZ 29.8.1926) married Israel Salzberger (after Aug 1926; no marriage in the Radautz index 1870-1929). They emigrated to Israel (Ramat-Aviv): 'In Ramat-Aviv: Dinah Salzberger, geb. Dollberg, früher Putna. Es trauern ihr Gatte Israel Salzberger, deren Ki[nder]...' (Die Stimme 1.5.1977 p.12). Dina died ~1977, survived by Israel and their children. Dina has no birth in the Radautz birth index (b.~1900 or earlier, born outside the registry towns or unindexed); her placement among the Putna Dollberg lines is open. The pattern: the Putna collections were run by Dollberg women paired with Salzberger men ('Salzberger - Dollberg' KKL committee 1924; Rosa Dollberg + Israel Salzberger Mar 1926; Dina Dollberg + Isak Salzberg Aug 1926).

Moses Dolberg (b.8-Mar-1882 Putna, P1110181): no marriage, no children, no death in the indexes; no press trace. David Dollberg (b.~1886 Putna): #2387 Dolberg David x Lindermann Ester, 22-Aug-1920, P1120461 (the family's only forward trace); no children (1921-1929), no death, no press. The 'Dr. Moses Dollberg' (advokat, Ehrenpräsident at the Emunah fraternity's 120th-semester celebration in Israel, Die Stimme 1.8.1963) is a DIFFERENT man - do not conflate. The Silka Maidanek x Salomon Dollberg line (m.1877) has no documented grandchildren in the Radautz indexes.

s20.isak_alper.s: Isak Alper (b.~1904) was an authorized orthopedic specialist / prosthetist of Czernowitz: 'Prothesen | Kunstbeine, Geh- und Stützapparate, Lederkorsette.. beim autorisierten orthopädischen Spezialisten Isak Alper - Czernowitz, Str. Podgoriei 6 (Weinberggasse)' (Morgenblatt 12.9.1931); 'Orthopäde ISAK ALPER geeicht!, beeideter Sachverständiger, Cernăuți, strada Stefan cel Mare 8' (Morgenblatt 25.12.1934). The prosthesis ads ran as a near-daily series through March-April 1936, then stop. Address timeline: Podgoriei 6 (1931) -> Ștefan cel Mare 8 (from Dec 1934). In June 1937, six months after marrying Fani Rosenblum (15.12.1936), he was advertising himself for ANY work ('Bin fleißig, gebildet, verläßlich, repräsentabel und sprachenkundig.. erbitte jedwede Verdienstermöglichung', Allg 23.6.1937). He died in Haifa ~April 1969 aged 65: 'In Haifa: Im Alter von 65 Jahren verschied Isak Alper, Orthopädist, früher Czernowitz. Es trauern seine Gattin Fanny Alper und die Tochter Ruth, verehl. Feiler.' (Die Stimme 1.5.1969).
s20.isak_alper.note: Q366-followup (R4). Routes: Yad Vashem 'Isak Alper'/'Fanny Alper'/'Ruth Feiler' (browser, Bar logins); MyHeritage Israel graves (Isak d.1969 Haifa - gravestone gives exact birth date); the 1936 Czernowitz marriage act (DAChO - names Fani's parents, the last direct test of the Peretz-x-Liza link).

s23.001.s: Israel Mortko's 1900 birth names his mother 'Klara Jurgrau, daughter of Salomon & Chane' - identical parentage to Chaje Odel (daughter of Salomon & Chane Freide) in the 1896/1901/1903 acts. Same parents = same woman; 'Klara' is a name variant (possibly also the burial record's 'Klara'). Agrees with the Q338 card's conclusion (mother = Chaje Odel).

s23.002.s: R4's 47-record harvest confirms the multi-wife pattern (s4.salomon_other_wives) and extends it: Feige (Edel) Fallenbaum's children Beile b.1.2.1877, Michael b.17.10.1879, Chaje Hudie b.16.4.1882 (Feige d.4.12.1888 aged 28); Lea Melzer's children Keile b.10.12.1889, Teme b.3.8.1891, civil marriage 26.9.1892. Whether all three wives belong to the SAME Salomon (Chaje Odel's father) stays OPEN.
s23.002.note: The children records are solid; the same-Salomon question is open.

s23.003.s: Chane Fride (Hana) nee Besner, 28 in 1874, daughter of Alter Besner x Miriam of Kimpolung/Campulung, resident of Oberhorodnik; civil marriage 29.12.1874; religious marriage earlier (Chaje Odel b.~1870). Corroborates Dad's Geni (s16.geni_fact_017, family says) with a record.

s23.004.s: Lifsche nee Jurgrau x Hersch Brender: their civil marriage was registered 12.09.1883 (vol. II, p.46/47, entry no.7) - remark on Leib Brender's 20.10.1862 birth entry. Children: Leib b.20.10.1862, Berl b.27.7.1866, Jankel b.25.6.1869, Meyer b.13.7.1875.

s23.005.s: Lifsche is likely Salomon's sister: Geni (S111, family says) has Lifsche as Chaim x Beile's daughter, and the 29.12.1874 marriage act (s19.haim_beila_parents) has Salomon as Haim x Beila's son. DECISIVE ROUTE still open: the 12.09.1883 marriage act P1120795 names Lifsche's parents (L248).
s23.005.note: Hypothesis kept; records + family says agree but the act is decisive.

s23.006.s: Hersch Brender had children with two women: Lifsche Jurgrau (Leib 1862, Berl 1866, Jankel 1869, Meyer 1875) and a Fischer woman (Jankel, Nuchem, Libe b.7.10.1878). Whether the Fischer children belong to the same Hersch or a different one is unresolved.

s23.007.s: The 'two Jankels' puzzle: Jankel Brender b.1869 (Hersch x Lifsche) died 16.3.1873 aged 3 (s18.jankel_brender_infancy), so the Fischer-wife Jankel is a later namesake reuse - or belongs to a different Hersch (kept open in s23.006).

s23.008.s: Radautz birth index: Michel Jurgrau b.14.1.1863, son of Chaim Jurgrau - corroborates Michel as Salomon's (half-)brother, i.e. Chaje Odel's uncle (KB note).

s23.009.s: Litman (Leiser Litman) Jurgrau b.~1845, d.1924; x Babi (Marjem Babzi) nee Brender (d.1924 aged 68; KB deaths index 'Marjem Babzi 1924'); children Jankel b.1.4.1875, Noe b.1.10.1876, Josef b.27.11.1879, Baßi b.26.6.1882, Schimschon b.4.11.1884, Berl b.12.8.1886, Nathan b.27.5.1888, Ester Malke b.11.1.1890.

s23.010.s: 7.3.1926 Ostjüdische Zeitung p.5: 'Fa. Litman Jurgrau 357' and 'Michel Jurgrau' in the Radautz KKL box-emptying list - Litman Jurgrau ran a Radautz business ('Fa.' = Firma).

s23.011.s: 21.6.1919 Ostjüdische Zeitung p.4: 'Sammlung Hochzeit Jurgrau - Nordmann' (wedding collection by Mendel Rosner and Brender; donors 'I. Jurgrau, K. Jurgrau') - the Jurgrau-Brender-Radautz milieu, no direct family link.

s23.012.s: DiFMOE 'Jurgrau' (340 hits) sampled: no press trace of Salomon/Chaje Odel's line specifically. Diaspora notices 'Blanka geb. Jurgrau' (wife of Dr. Misiu Lenczner, Toronto) and 'Ing. Abraham Jurgrau, früher Gurahumora - Czernowitz' (1.10.1976 Die Stimme p.12) are NOT our family (negative).
