s25.001.s: The younger Joel Maidanek was born in November 1858 in Zaleszczyki, son of Maier Maidanek of Zaleszczyki; he was a merchant (Kaufmann) in Radautz. The detail fragment P1120186 likewise names him 'Joel Maidanek, son of Maier Maidanek'. (His mother's name is read 'Jente' [?] in the 1909 act.)
s25.001.note: Tightens the birth estimate on n_joel2_zwik (was ~1865-1880). Mother Jente read with [?] - not asserted beyond the act reading.

s25.002.s: In his civil marriage act of 28.7.1909 (Radautz), Joel Maidanek signed a declaration legitimating the children born to Chaje Sure before the marriage; the note names the years 1888, 1891 and 1896 and a 'Malke Grete' [?]. The bride, Chaje Sure Zwik [?] (surname also read 'Zwirn'), was born May 1862 in Zaleszczyki, daughter of Hersch Zwik [?] and Rifke Zwik [?] of Zaleszczyki.
s25.002.note: The marriage itself is already confirmed (s20.joel2, from the index); this act image adds the legitimation declaration and the bride data. The declaration note is only partly legible.

s25.003.s: Malke Golde Maidanek was born 17.9.1888 in Zwiniacze [?], daughter of Joel Maidanek and Chaje, residing in Radautz (her 1909 marriage act, P1120199 no.67, citing her birth certificate of 1905).
s25.003.note: Birthplace reading [?]; birth date and parentage read clean. She is one of the children legitimated in her parents 1909 act (s25.002).

s25.004.s: Malke Golde Maidanek married Joachim Ellenbogen in Radautz in December 1909 (the act annotation dates it 24.12.1909 [?]); officiant Simon Schapira.
s25.004.note: Exact day rests on the annotation reading [?].

s25.005.s: Joachim Ellenbogen, of Radautz, was born 12.12.1878 [?], son of Salomon Ellenbogen and Chaje.
s25.005.note: Birth year and the mother name carry [?] in the transcription.

s25.006.s: Juda Josef Maidanek was born 14.6.1896 in Radautz (house 85), son of Joel Madanik (surname written 'Madanik'; occupation read [?]wirth, possibly innkeeper) of Radautz and of Chaje Sore (her surname in the act is only partly read, 'Kur...k' [?]).
s25.006.note: Birth date, place and father read clean; the mother surname and the father occupation carry [?]. Corroborates the existing birth data on this person.

s25.007.s: Chaim Alter Maidanek married Adela Drukman on 2.5.1906 at Oberwikow. The bride, born 25.6.1881 (per her birth certificate), was the legitimate daughter of Jakob Drukman and Rosa Drukman of Dorna Kandreni and the widow of Chaim Gronich (d. 12.4.1904 at Kimpelung). Officiant: R. Israel Harnik of Oberwikow.
s25.007.note: Bride birthplace read “Rosna” [?] (district Kimpelung) - place name only is uncertain. The marriage was known; the act image is now in hand.

s25.008.s: The 1906 marriage act names Chaim Alter Maidanek as the legitimate son of the deceased David Maidanek and of Debora Maidanek of Radautz, born 1875 in Unterwikow (per his Heimatschein), merchant in Oberwikow. This is the David Maidanek who married Devora Rosenberg in 1876 - Chaim Alter is their son.
s25.008.note: Firms the link the consolidated note flagged as “to verify”: the act states the parentage directly.

s25.009.s: The marriage act of Moses Meidenek and Marie Maidanek (Radautz marriage register vol. II, pp.32-33, entry 26; image P1120788) gives the groom as 24, son of [father name not read in this transcription] and Sura, of Budna [?], and the bride as Marie Maidanek, 23, daughter of David Maidanek of Radautz. The act carries a legitimation note for the couple's daughter Mina, and a later Romanian annotation records that the bride died at Czernowitz (Cernauti) on 12.2.1930, death register no.187/1930.
s25.009.note: Same act as the stage-15 reading (docs W90-W93), which read the father as Leiser and the place as Putna, and dated the spread January 1881 (13.1.1881); this delivery transcription dated the spread January 1880 and could not read the father name. The two readings are of one act; the year header should be re-checked on a zoom, but no conflict is opened on a header reading.

s25.010.s: Chaje Bince Meidanek married Moses Schwirz at Oberwikow in May-June 1904 (act dated by the banns; the father written consent is dated Radautz 31.5.1904 and signed 'Moses Maidanek'). The groom, born 2.10.1877 in Unterstanestie, was the legitimate son of Michael Schwirz and Eidel Schwirz nee Grill of Unterstanestie, merchant residing there.
s25.010.note: The existing note “m. Moses Schwitz 31.5.1904” took the consent date as the marriage date; the act itself is a May-June 1904 marriage (a day, possibly the 21st [?], is written out). Groom surname written Schwirz.

s25.011.s: The 1904 marriage act names Chaje Bince Meidanek (written 'Meidanek'; her father 'Maidanek'), residing in Radautz, as the legitimate daughter of Moses Maidanek of Oberwikow and of Marie Maidanek of Oberwikow, born 13.1.1881 per the birth register.
s25.011.note: Corroborates the birth-index parentage (s9.moses_marie_children) from the act itself.

s25.012.s: Rifka Maidanek (b.1877, of Radautz) married Josef Peritz [?] on 9.4.1900 in Radautz (officiant David Maier [?]). The act names her father as Mordche [?] Maidanek of Oberwikow, house no.380.
s25.012.note: CAREFUL: the KB birth-index parentage for Rifka (b.24.8.1877) is Moses + Marie Meidanek (s9.moses_marie_children). The act father reading “Mordche” carries a [?] and may be a misread; parentage is NOT reassigned on this reading alone. The groom surname Peritz also carries a [?].

s25.013.s: Jeni Gisele was born in November 1905 (day spelled out, read '23rd' [?]) at Oberwikow, house 380, legitimate daughter of Moses Schmil [?] and of Chaje, residing in Oberwikow, daughter of Mirjam Maidanek of Oberwikow.
s25.013.note: Father cell largely illegible in the photo; the mother and grandmother readings are the usable content.

s25.014.s: Seti [?] (the name may read 'Peti') was born in December 1908 at Oberwikow, house 380, daughter of Chaje Pince [?], residing in Oberwikow, legitimate daughter of Jakob Wolf Schaechter [?] and of Marie Maidanek of Oberwikow.
s25.014.note: Same mother and same house 380 as Jeni Gisele (1905) - the two girls are sisters. The grandfather surname “Schaechter” carries a [?].

s25.015.s: Chaje of Oberwikow house 380, mother of Jeni Gisele (b.1905) and Seti [?] (b.1908) by Moses Schmil [?], was a daughter of Marie (in the 1905 act: Mirjam) Maidanek of Oberwikow; the 1908 act names her father as Jakob Wolf Schaechter [?]. House 380 is also the house given for the Maidanek father in Rifka Maidanek 1900 marriage act (P1120475 no.9) - a possible kinship cluster around house 380, not proven.
s25.015.note: Entered as kinship context only; no parent link to Marie (wife of Moses) is asserted - whether this Marie/Mirjam Maidanek is the same woman is open.

s25.016.s: Israel Mortko birth act itself is now photographed (P1100860 no.28): born 18.2.1900 at Oberhorodnik house 476; the mother column names Klara Jurgrau, daughter of Salomon + Chane Jurgrau; the father is named in the annotation as Abraham Majdanek of Oberhorodnik, with the note that the parents lived in a religious-only ('illegaler Ehe') marriage; the annotation records the child death on 27.5.1900.
s25.016.note: Day discrepancy stands: the death register (P1140893, Edo claim israel_death) read the death as 25.5.1900; the birth-act annotation reads 27/5 1900. Month/year and the Klara = Chaje Odel parentage agree with stage 23.

s25.017.s: Chane Feive [?] Maidanek birth act is now photographed (P1100640 no.6): born January 1905 at Oberhorodnik house 476, daughter of Abraham Maidanek and of Chaje Orel [?] - the act parents-marriage reference (Trauungsmatrik Tom II f.71/72, married 3.10.1901) is Abraham x Chaje Odel civil marriage, so 'Orel' is read as Odel. The mother column adds that Chaje mother was Chane Frive [?] Besner of Oberhorodnik.
s25.017.note: Corroborates stage 23/24 readings of this birth from the index and the highlighted photo; the name readings (Feive, Orel, Frive) carry [?].

s25.018.s: A man surnamed Majdanek (surname zoom-verified in the register photo; first name illegible) died on 2.6.1860 at house 1059, aged 65 (born ~1795), cause read as Altersschwaeche [?] (senility). Latin-form death register (IMG_6968). Earliest Maidanek record in the KB so far.
s25.018.note: Entered exactly as the tasking for this delivery requires: unknown-first-name person, status partly. Cf. Q219 (the 1860 death act route).

s25.019.s: Malze (Malca) Brender 1928 marriage act (P1120089 no.45) states she was born 11.2.1904 in Radautz and is the legitimate daughter of David Brender, merchant in Radautz, and of Beile nee Margulies, in Radautz.
s25.019.note: One of the two pillars of the Margulies reading in Q066 (see s25.023 and conflict X54).

s25.020.s: Malze (Malca) Brender married Josef-Isac Scholder on 19.7.1928 in Radauti; officiant chief rabbi Dr. Iacob Nacht. The groom, born 16.5.1901 in Radauti, baker in Radauti, is the legitimate son of Israel-Wolf Scholder, tailor [?], and of Chane nee Weber, of Radauti.
s25.020.note: The Brender-Scholder wedding also appears in the 1928 press (Q315/Q080 thread).

s25.021.s: David Brender, 24, ledig, of Radautz, married Beile, 20, ledig, on 25.11.1890 in Radautz (marriage register entry 32; officiant Jean Kupfer [?]). The groom father name is not legible in the photo.
s25.021.note: Date and couple read clean. The bride's maiden name (Q066) was resolved 17.10.2026: Schapira - see s25.022 (confirmed), s25.023 (annotated) and X54 (resolved).

s25.022.s: Q066 reading A (Schapira) - CONFIRMED by the zoom re-read of 17.10.2026: in David Brender's own marriage act of 25.11.1890 (P1120822 no.32), the bride is Beila Schapira, born in Cseres, daughter of Moses Schapira and Rachel Margulies of Radautz. Beile's maiden name is Schapira.
s25.022.note: Originally entered as an uncertain Kurrent reading (stage 25). The zoom re-read of R25_030 settled it - see conflict X54 (resolved, stage 27). Matches the family tree (S111): Beile Schapira, daughter of Elias-Moses Schapira x Rachel Margulies.

s25.023.s: Q066 reading B (Margulies): the 1928 Scholder marriage act (P1120089 no.45) names David Brender wife expressly as 'Beile nee Margulies', and the birth-index details for the couple children Malca (b.1904) and Morris (b.1906) likewise give the mother maiden name as Margulies.
s25.023.note: Strong, but indirect for the 1890 bride herself: it names David wife in 1928 and the children mother in 1904/1906. With s25.022 it forms conflict X54; Q066 is PARTLY ANSWERED - a zoom re-read of the 1890 bride column decides it (or the two-wives possibility, both named Beile, remains). RESOLVED 17.10.2026 (stage 27): the 1890 act's parental column shows Margulies was Beile's mother Rachel's family name, carried into the mother's slot in these later records - the record statements stand as written; the maiden name itself is Schapira (s25.022, X54 resolved).

s25.024.s: Q285 - THE ACT IS IN HAND: Maier Kurzberg, born 18.6.1877 in Wiznitz, married Heri Lea Raful (born ~1881 [?], Radautz) on 14.11.1901 in Radautz - Radautz marriage register Book 3, pp.95-96, entry 122, image P1120073. This also resolves the image-number muddle: the act is P1120073 (delivered by Hauster under the label of the 1928 Ellenbogen x Brender act), NOT P1120516 as the index cross-reference said, and NOT P1120526 (an unrelated births page).
s25.024.note: Corroborates s22.021 / s22.042 (index-based) from the act itself. Parents names in the act columns need a careful second read - not entered.

s25.025.s: A second Raful bride in the same register spread: Scheindel Raful married a groom from Ober-Wikow [?] on 24.11.1901 (Radautz marriage register Book 3, entry 121, image P1120073).
s25.025.note: First-pass read (batch-MINE); the groom is unnamed in it and the entry numbering 121/122 may swap - a second read of the page would firm this up.

s25.026.s: Marjem Batzi Brender, 36, born in Czernowitz [?], daughter of the deceased [?] Brender of Radautz, married in Radautz in December 1892 (the act day word reads the 24th [?]; the published index gives 27.12.1892). The groom, 39, of Radautz, is read in the act as [?] Junger (given name read 'Josef' [?]); the index names the groom 'Lipman'. The act carries a long legitimation-type annotation mentioning the years 1882/1886 and Abraham [?], only partly legible.
s25.026.note: Age 36 in Dec 1892 fits Babi (Marjem Babzi) Brender, b.~1856, wife of Litman (Leiser Litman) Jurgrau. If the groom is in fact Litman Jurgrau, this would be the civil registration of that marriage - NOT asserted: the act groom surname reads Junger [?], and the identification stays open.

s25.027.s: Lea Feldhammer (born 1874, legitimate daughter of Salomon [?] Feldhammer of Radautz) married Chaim Zibener [?] (born 1860) on 10.12.1901 in Radautz (marriage register pp.127/128, entry 173; witnesses Moses Kohn and Hersch Rosen [?] of Radautz).
s25.027.note: Groom surname and the father first name carry [?]. The father Salomon [?] is plausibly the Salomon Feldhammer of the Q286 cohort note - the reading is not firm enough to link the persons.

s25.028.s: Gitel Feldhammer (born 1868, daughter of Salomon [?] Feldhammer [?]) married Itzig Schachter (born 1866, son of Moritz [?] Schachter [?]) on 7.4.1902 at Putna (marriage register fol.167/168, entry 56). The bride is given as of 'Maydan' [?].
s25.028.note: Couple and date read clean; both fathers names carry [?].

s25.029.s: Ettie Golde Laufer, 38, born in Oberwikow [?], daughter of Mordko Leib Laufer and Lea Laufer of Oberwikow, married Josef Kurzberg, 42, born in Wisznitz, residing in Oberwikow (house 926 [?]), in January of the 1880/81 register spread (vol. II pp.32-33, entry 29; image P1120788).
s25.029.note: Bride and her parentage agree in both transcriptions of this page. Two readings differ: this delivery reads the groom as Josef Kurzberg and the spread as Jan 1880; the stage-15 overview read the groom given name as “Noach” and the spread as Jan 1881. Groom given name and year stay partly until a zoom re-read.

s25.030.s: Mordko Leib Laufer, 72, widower, farmer (Grundwirth) residing in Radautz, son of the late Chaim Laufer and Beila [?] Laufer of Radautz, married Lea Hersch [?], 72, daughter of Josef Hersch [?] and Ettel Hersch [?] of Radautz, in 1890 (marriage register pp.96-97, entry 17; an annotation mentions 28.6.1890 [?]). Witnesses: Rosa Kurzberg of Oberwikow and Simon Metscher [?] of Radautz.
s25.030.note: Ages and the groom parentage read clean; the bride surname and the exact date carry [?]. This is the same Mordko Leib Laufer whose daughter Ettie Golde married in entry P1120788 no.29.

s25.031.s: Efroim Laufer, butcher [?] (Fleischhauer) of Radautz, son of [?] Laufer, married [?] Hover [?] (first name partly illegible, read 'Eni' [?]), daughter of [?] Hover of Radautz, on 27.2.1876 (bilingual marriage register, entry 55, house 1109; officiant Hersch Schapira). On the same page (entry 52, 18.8.1875) a Chaim Laufer of Radautz appears as a witness.
s25.031.note: Bride name and the groom occupation carry [?]; couple, date and house number read clean.

s25.032.s: Efroim Laufer, son of Abraham Laufer of Radautz, died 1.12.1887 in Radautz (house 1109 [?]) aged 6 and was buried 2.12.1887 (death register entry 135, death-inspection certificate Radautz 2.12.1887 no.397; cause Fraisen per the continuation page).
s25.032.note: Name, father, dates and age read clean. The continuation page sex mark appears female, which conflicts with the name Efroim - recorded as written; the continuation-column alignment is uncertain and the name/father/date are not in doubt.

s25.033.s: Samuel Laufer [?], born 1854, of Stukow/Sukow [?], son of Mordche [?] Laufer [?], married Chane (Chana) Hochman [?], born 1854, daughter of Menasche [?] and Drane [?] Hochman [?], on 8.4.1902 [?] at Oberwikow (marriage register fol.167/168, entry 58).
s25.033.note: Nearly every reading in this entry carries a [?] - entered so the act is on record, at low confidence.

s25.034.s: Mendel, son of Chaim [surname partly illegible, read 'Seidman/Seurman' [?]] (Mortko) of Radautz and of Hinde Laufer, daughter of Nussen [?] Laufer, was born in February 1900 in Radautz (house 971). A later Romanian annotation in the birth act records: deceased, death act no.330 of 10.2.1972, registered in Bucharest.
s25.034.note: Mother identity and the 1972 Bucharest death annotation read clean; the father surname does not.

s25.035.s: The marriage act of Schloime (Salomon) Jurgrau and Chane Bosner is now photographed (IMG_5417 no.41): banns 12/19/26.12.1874, civil marriage 29.12.1874, at house no.1 in Ober-Horodnik [?]. The groom, an innkeeper [?] (Schanker), is the son of Chaim Jurgrau and Beile Jurgrau (mother deceased); the bride is the daughter of Alter Bosner and Marjem Bosner of Kimpelung (Campulung), residing in Ober-Horodnik [?]. Witnesses: Mendel Saldriger [?] and Hersch Brender, both of Radautz. Officiant Hersch Schapira.
s25.035.note: Corroborates from the act itself the marriage already in the KB from the index harvest (chane.2; s23.003). Ages (groom 29 [?], bride 30 [?]) and the place name carry [?].

s25.036.s: Schewe (Scheine) Jurgrau, 24, ledig, of Radautz, legitimate daughter of Jossel and Roma Jurgrau of Radautz, married Chaim Sternschuss [?], 23 [?], ledig, son of Aba and Brundel Sternschuss of Zaleszczyki, on 27.6.1877 in Radautz (bilingual marriage register pp.64-65, entry 37, house 1342; officiant Hersch Schapira).
s25.036.note: Bride, parentage and date read clean; the groom surname and his age carry [?].

s25.037.s: The 29.4.1877 marriage act of Mendel Besner is now photographed (IMG_5437 entry 18): Mendel Besner, of Bilke [?], son of [father name illegible] and Gaje Besner of Radautz, married [?] Habermann - her first name is obscured by an ink blot (possibly Feige [?]) - daughter of Abraham and Chaje Habermann (both deceased), residing in Bilke. All five entries on the page were married 29.4.1877; officiant Hersch Schapira.
s25.037.note: The KB (index/family) names the wife Sluwe Devora Habermann (cf. person n_sluwe_devora_habermann); this photo cannot confirm her first name - the blot sits exactly on it. Couple, date and both families read clean.

s25.038.s: Moses Besner, born 1890 in Andrasfalva [?] (on a day no longer determinable), merchant there, legitimate son of Jankel Besner [?] and Ruchel Glendel [?] nee Eigenstein [?], married Ester Ruchel Besner [?], born 25.11.1895 in Radautz, legitimate daughter of Itzig Besner [?], merchant in Radautz, and of Debora nee Schachter, on 16.11.1920 in Radauti (officiant Dr. Jakob Hoffmann; witnesses Mendel Sterlin and Nute Schachter, merchants of Radauti).
s25.038.note: Couple and date read clean; several parent names carry [?], and the bride surname is cut in the page gutter.

s25.039.s: NEGATIVE (Vicov register): answering Bar request of 10.10.2026, Edgar Hauster searched the Vicov (Vicovu) birth register and reported on 15.10.2026: 'There are no entries for Mendel Maidanek + Adolf/Josef Maidanek in the Vicov Register.' Mendel (b.1898) and Adolf/Josef Maidanek (b.1884/1887) births were therefore registered elsewhere, not at Vicov.
s25.039.note: CORRECTION to the consolidated Inbox note of 15.10.2026, whose “still missing” section wrongly listed the Vicov birth images as undelivered - Hauster did answer, with this negative result. Mendel birth act is in any case already in hand from the Radautz register (D04). No lead is opened for Vicov; the route is closed.

s26.001.s: Perla Rosenblum's birth was registered at Iasi with act no. 596, act date 10 May 1879 (alphabetical birth index for 1879, folio 457v - the same folio that carries Peretz Rosenblum's act 2164 entry).
s26.001.note: Read directly from the archive photocopy by Bar and Bob, 15.10.2026. The index gives the act date; the birth itself may be days earlier. No parents are named in an alphabetical index.

s26.002.s: Relationship to Peretz Rosenblum unknown. HYPOTHESIS: a sister or cousin - two Rosenblum births registered at Iasi five weeks apart in spring 1879 (Peretz 12.4, Perla 10.5) point to one extended family in the city. Her birth act (596/1879, via the Iasi Civil Status Service / SJAN follow-up of 15.10.2026) would name her parents and settle it.
s26.002.note: No relationship row is created until a record names her parents. Do not merge with any other Perla/Perl in the tree.
cit: DSC_1671 folio 457v, acts 2164 and 596 on one folio

s26.003.s: On the archive's own photocopy of the 1879 alphabetical birth index (folio 457v), Peretz's entry is added in violet ink as act 2164 with act date 12 April 1879 and the observation 'Trans. 1950' - the act was transcribed in 1950, which is why SJAN Iasi does not hold it; the act sits with the Iasi Civil Status Service (asked 15.10.2026).
s26.003.note: Supports peretz.0 (born 12.4.1879, act 2164), which stays "partly": the index column is the act date (DATA ACTULUI), and the underlying act has not been sighted yet.

s27.001.s: Chunne (Chune) Ellenbogen was born 28 December 1894 in Gura Humorului (his 1928 Radautz marriage act, citing his birth act: Gura Humorului vol. II p.156 no.72).
s27.001.note: Fills the previously empty birth data on n_chunne_ellenbogen.

s27.002.s: Chunne Ellenbogen's 1928 marriage act enters him as the illegitimate son of Gittel Ellenbogen and Benjamin-Wolf Ellenbogen, both of Gura Humorului - i.e. his parents were not civilly married when he was born.
s27.002.note: Parentage as written in the act. The father is not merged with either Geni-import Benjamin (g16_0117 / g16_0118) on this evidence alone.

s27.003.s: In 1928 Chunne Ellenbogen was an industrialist (factory owner) residing in Radautz (his marriage act); the act's annotations also cite his military booklet - Bat. 11 Vanatori de Munte, matricola 574/916.

s27.004.s: The marriage act itself (Radautz, 29.2.1928, Trauungsmatrik Tom II pp.515-516 no.14): Rebeca Brender married Chunne Ellenbogen before Chief Rabbi Dr. Iacob Nacht; witnesses Hers-Ber Klugacs [?] (beadle) and Hers Storper (merchant); the act cites the bride's birth entry (vol. VI pp.9/10 no.4) and a rabbinate marriage notification dated 1.3.1928. A partly legible later marginal note appears to record a marriage certificate issued 1.11.1952 [?] and an annulment [?] of the marriage.
s27.004.note: The act confirms s19.rebeka_chunne_marriage (index-based) and s18.rebeca_pesach_not_berl (the act names her legitimate daughter of Pesach Brender + Lea nascuta Brender). Only the 1952/annulment marginalia are [?] readings - hence partly. The annulment, if real, is a new fact about the marriage worth a follow-up read of the marginal note.
